framework: Maine state academic standards: Health Education
subject: Health Education

source.publisher: Maine state education agency (machine-readable via Common Standards Project / ASN)

units.title: Health Concepts: Students comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health

outcomes.text: Students recognize that healthy behaviors impact personal health.
Students recognize that there are multiple dimensions of health.
Students describe the transmission and prevention of common childhood communicable diseases.
Students describe ways a safe and healthy school environment can promote personal health.
Students identify basic health terms related to family life; nutrition; personal health; safety and injury prevention; and tobacco, alcohol, and other drug use prevention.

units.title: Health Information, Products and Services: Students demonstrate the ability to access valid health information, services, and products to enhance health

outcomes.text: Students identify trusted adults and professionals who can help promote health.
Students identify ways to locate school and community health helpers.

units.title: Health Promotion and Risk Reduction: Students demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate age-appropriate healthy practices to maintain or improve personal health

outcomes.text: Choose healthy foods.
Demonstrate personal hygiene skills, including hand-washing.

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate behaviors to avoid or reduce personal health risks

outcomes.text: Demonstrate a variety of safety skills for different situations.
Differentiate between safe and harmful substances found at home and school.
Recognize basic signs, symbols, and warning labels for health and safety.
Students demonstrate coping strategies to use when feeling too excited, anxious, upset, angry, or out of control.

units.title: Influences on Health: Students analyze the ability of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors to enhance health

subtopics.title: Students identify influences on personal health practices and behaviors

outcomes.text: Identify family influences on personal health practices and behaviors.
Identify what the school can do to support personal health practices and behaviors.
Describe how the media can influence health behaviors.

units.title: Communication and Advocacy Skills: Students demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication and advocacy skills to enhance personal, family, and community health

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate healthy ways to communicate

outcomes.text: Demonstrate healthy ways to express needs, wants, and feelings.
Distinguish between verbal and nonverbal communication.
Make requests to promote personal health.
Demonstrate listening skills to enhance health.
Demonstrate ways to respond to an unwanted, threatening, or dangerous situation including telling a trusted adult if threatened or harmed.
Students encourage peers to make positive health choices.

units.title: Decision-Making and Goal-Setting Skills: Students demonstrate the ability to make decisions and set goals to enhance health

subtopics.title: Students identify situations where a health-related decision is needed

outcomes.text: Differentiate between situations when health-related decisions can appropriately be made by the individual and when assistance is needed.
Students identify a short-term personal health goal and take action toward achieving the goal.

units.title: Movement/Motor Skills and Knowledge: Students demonstrate the fundamental and specialized movement skills and apply principles of movement for improved performance

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate positions that create stability and force

outcomes.text: Show how base of support changes during static balances.
Demonstrate how body position can be adapted to pushing and pulling forces.
Demonstrate how to lift objects to prevent injuries.

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate a variety of locomotor skills

outcomes.text: Demonstrate correct technique for a variety of locomotor skills.
Demonstrate a locomotor skill applying changes in direction, level, and/or pathway.
Demonstrate combinations of locomotor skills.
Students identify the skill-related fitness components of balance and coordination.

units.title: Physical Fitness Activities and Knowledge: Students demonstrate and apply fitness concepts

outcomes.text: Students identify components of health-related fitness.
Students participate in physical activities to introduce the health-related fitness components of flexibility, cardiovascular endurance, muscular endurance, and muscular strength.
Students identify the physical benefits and bodily responses related to physical activities.

units.title: Personal and Social Skills and Knowledge: Students demonstrate and explain responsible personal behavior and responsible social behavior in physical activity settings

outcomes.text: Students demonstrate taking turns and sharing while participating in physical activities.
Students follow procedures for safe behaviors, including maintaining appropriate personal space, while participating in physical activities.

subtopics.title: Safety Rules and Rules of Play

outcomes.text: Students identify safety rules and rule of play for games/physical activities.

outcomes.text: Students explain the relationship between healthy behaviors and personal health.

outcomes.text: Students identify characteristics of valid health information, products, and services.
Students locate resources from home, school, and the community that provide valid health information.

outcomes.text: Design healthy menus.
Demonstrate basic care of the human body.

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate a variety of behaviors to avoid or reduce personal health risks

outcomes.text: Demonstrate healthy and safe ways to recognize, deal with, or avoid threatening situations.
Develop injury prevention and safety strategies for personal health.

units.title: Influences on Health: Students analyze the ability of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors to enhance health

subtopics.title: Students describe how a variety of factors influence personal health behaviors

outcomes.text: Describe how family, school, and community influence and support personal health practices and behaviors.
Describe how peers and culture can influence health practices and behaviors.
Explain how media influences thoughts, feelings, and health behaviors.
Students describe ways technology can influence personal health.

units.title: Communication and Advocacy Skills: Students demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication and advocacy skills to enhance personal, family, and community health

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate effective verbal and nonverbal interpersonal communication skills to enhance health

outcomes.text: Demonstrate appropriate listening skills to enhance health.
Demonstrate effective verbal and non-verbal communication skills including assertiveness skills to enhance health.
Demonstrate how to ask for assistance to enhance personal health.
Demonstrate refusal skills to avoid or reduce health risks.
Demonstrate non-violent strategies to manage or resolve conflict.

subtopics.title: Students encourage others to make positive health choices

outcomes.text: Express opinions about health issues.

units.title: Decision-Making and Goal-Setting Skills: Students demonstrate the ability to make decisions and set goals to enhance health

subtopics.title: Students apply decision-making steps to enhance health

outcomes.text: Identify health-related situations that might require a thoughtful decision.
List healthy options to health-related issues or problems and predict the potential outcomes of each option when making a health-related decision.
Choose a healthy option when making a decision.
Describe the outcome of a health-related decision.

subtopics.title: Students utilize goal-setting skills to implement a short-term personal health goal

outcomes.text: Set a short-term personal health goal.
Identify resources to assist in achieving the health goal.
Track progress toward achieving the goal.

units.title: Movement/Motor Skills and Knowledge: Students demonstrate the fundamental and specialized movement skills and apply principles of movement for improved performance

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate a variety of movements that apply stability and force

outcomes.text: Demonstrate movements that change the center of gravity and line of gravity during dynamic balances.
Show how increasing speed and mass can change the force on an object.
Demonstrate how body position can be changed to absorb force and decrease risk for injury.

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate a variety of locomotor skills and manipulative skills

outcomes.text: Demonstrate correct technique for a variety of manipulative skills.
Demonstrate locomotor skills and manipulative skills in combination using changes in direction, level, or pathway.
Students identify the skill-related fitness components of balance, coordination, agility, and speed.
Students describe why practice is important to skill improvement.

units.title: Physical Fitness Activities and Knowledge: Students demonstrate and apply fitness concepts

outcomes.text: Students participate in multiple health-related fitness assessments (including a cardiovascular assessment) and reassess to observe changes over time.
Students describe and give examples of the five health-related fitness components.

Students participate in physical activities that address each of the five health-related fitness components including flexibility, cardiovascular endurance, muscular endurance, muscular strength, and body composition.
Students identify physical and mental benefits and bodily responses related to regular participation in physical activity.

units.title: Health Concepts: Students comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health

subtopics.title: Students examine the relationship between behaviors and personal health

outcomes.text: Explain the importance of assuming responsibility for personal health.

subtopics.title: Students determine how environment and other factors impact personal health

units.title: Health Information, Products and Services: Students demonstrate the ability to access valid health information, services, and products to enhance health

outcomes.text: Students analyze the validity of health information, products, and services.

subtopics.title: Students locate valid and reliable health information, products, and services

outcomes.text: Explain situations requiring the use of valid and reliable health information, products, and services.

units.title: Health Promotion and Risk Reduction: Students demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks

outcomes.text: Students demonstrate a healthy practice and/or behavior to maintain or improve their own health in each of the following areas: personal hygiene, healthy eating; physical activity; and tobacco, alcohol, and other drug use prevention.

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate behaviors to avoid or reduce health risks to self and others

outcomes.text: Demonstrate ways to recognize, avoid, or change situations that threaten the safety of self and others.
Develop injury prevention and response strategies including first aid for personal and family health.
Students distinguish between healthy and unhealthy strategies for stress, anger, and grief management.

units.title: Influences on Health: Students analyze the ability of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors to enhance health

subtopics.title: Students explain and analyze influences on adolescent health behaviors

outcomes.text: Examine how the family, school, and community influence the health behaviors of adolescents.
Describe how peers influence healthy and unhealthy behaviors.
Analyze how messages from media influence health behaviors.
Explain how the perceptions of norms influence healthy and unhealthy behaviors.
Explain how culture and personal values and beliefs influence individual health behaviors.
Students analyze the influence of technology, including medical technology, on personal and family health.

subtopics.title: Students describe how some health risk behaviors can influence the likelihood of engaging in unhealthy behaviors

outcomes.text: Describe how gateway drugs can lead to the use of other drugs.
Describe the influence of alcohol and other drug use on judgment and self-control.

units.title: Communication and Advocacy Skills: Students demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication and advocacy skills to enhance personal, family, and community health

subtopics.title: Students apply effective verbal and nonverbal interpersonal communication skills to enhance health

outcomes.text: Demonstrate communication skills to build and maintain healthy relationships.
Demonstrate effective communication skills including asking for assistance to enhance the health of self and others.
Demonstrate refusal and negotiation skills to avoid or reduce health risks.
Demonstrate effective conflict management or conflict resolution strategies.

subtopics.title: Students describe ways to influence and support others in making positive health choices

outcomes.text: Develop a health-enhancing position on a topic and support it with information.
Develop health-enhancing messages using communication techniques that target a specific audience.
Demonstrate an ability to work cooperatively as an advocate for healthy individuals, families, and schools.

units.title: Decision-Making and Goal-Setting Skills: Students demonstrate the ability to make decisions and set goals to enhance health

subtopics.title: Students apply decision-making skills to enhance health

outcomes.text: Determine when health-related situations require the application of a thoughtful decision-making process.
Determine when individual or collaborative decision-making is appropriate.
Distinguish between healthy and unhealthy alternatives to health-related issues or problems and predict the potential short-term impact of alternative decisions for themselves and others.
Choose healthy alternatives over unhealthy alternatives when making a decision.
Analyze the outcomes of a health-related decision.

subtopics.title: Students develop and apply strategies to attain a short-term personal health goal

outcomes.text: Assess personal health practices.
Develop a short-term goal to adopt, maintain, or improve a personal health practice.
Develop and apply strategies and monitor progress toward a personal health goal.
Describe how personal health goals can vary with changing abilities, priorities, and responsibilities.

units.title: Movement/Motor Skills and Knowledge: Students demonstrate the fundamental and specialized movement skills and apply principles of movement for improved performance

subtopics.title: Students change their motion and the motion of objects by applying the principles of stability and force during skill practice

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the principle of opposition.
Demonstrate how the point of contact changes the path of an object.
Demonstrate how the point of release changes the path of an object.
Demonstrate lifts and actions that decrease risk for injury.

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate motor skills and manipulative skills during drills or modified games/physical activities

outcomes.text: Demonstrate correct technique for motor skills and manipulative skills during drills or modified games/physical activities.
Combine manipulative skills with motor skills during drills or modified games/physical activities.
Students describe the following skill-related fitness components: balance, coordination, agility, speed, and power.
Students explain how specific, positive, and correct feedback affect skill improvement.

units.title: Physical Fitness Activities and Knowledge: Students demonstrate and apply fitness concepts

outcomes.text: Students participate in a health-related fitness assessment that addresses a variety of health-related fitness components to establish personal fitness goals.
Students design a fitness program from established goals which addresses the five health-related fitness components and applies the frequency, intensity, time, and type (FITT) guidelines.

Students participate in physical activities that address personal fitness goals for the health-related fitness components including flexibility, cardiovascular endurance, muscular endurance, muscular strength, and body composition.
Students describe physiological responses and physical, mental/intellectual, emotional, and social benefits related to regular participation in physical activity.

Analyze how peers influence healthy and unhealthy behaviors.
Evaluate the effect of the media on personal and family health.

Analyze how culture and personal values and beliefs influence individual health behaviors.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate effective communication skills including asking for and offering assistance to enhance the health of self and others.

outcomes.text: Compare the value of thoughtful decision-making to quick decision-making in a health-related situation.
Justify when individual or collaborative decision-making is appropriate.
